summary:
During space missions, astronauts face significant health risks due to microgravity, cosmic radiation, isolation, and confined living environments. Continuously monitoring astronauts' health and detecting potential medical risks at an early stage are essential to ensuring their well-being during spaceflight so that space missions can continue and advance without any prejudice of the society. 
ASTRO-SKIN is a concept comprising a smart astronaut suit and a mobile application, developed to continuously monitor the health status of astronauts and their surrounding environmental conditions during space missions which provides momentary and long term data to follow up each astronaut’s well being and solutions that astronauts can apply independent from the Earth when needed. However, ASTRO-SKIN introduces an additional technological layer by integrating united sensors that measure each condition from the astronaut’s clothing. After gathering these informations ASTRO-SKIN application forms momentary graphic and charts to provide the astronaut a guide and sends these charts to Earth offline. The application includes components such as a Holistic Health Cockpit, an AI-driven Diagnostic and SANS module, an Environmental and Radiation Dosimetry module, and a Physio/ExIS module. Through AI-powered analysis and early warning alerts the system assists in identifying potential health issues, plans to prevent  modalizes solutions for them.
details: ASTRO-SKIN is a health-monitoring and mission-support system designed to make space travel safer and more efficient especially for long missions where astronauts face many challenges. The system combines a wearable garment with a digital platform to help monitor health and support missions. The wearable part, called ASTRO-SKIN has sensors that track things like heart rate, breathing, body temperature, movement and humidity. These sensors help keep track of how the astronaut's doing and the environment inside the suit. The sensors connect to a processing unit that sends the data to the platform. The design of the garment also includes layers that protect and keep the astronaut comfortable. The project also looks at ways to use accessories for health monitoring. The digital platform turns the data into a place where astronauts and mission teams can see health info check trends monitor the spaceship and practice emergency steps. The main part of the platform has five areas: Overview, Workout, Flight, Systems and Missions. The Overview area shows health data. Allows users to look at different time ranges of live, short-term and long-term. There are graphs and progress bars to help track health. The Workout section includes fun training activities that help with fitness and mental health. The Flight section connects health data to spaceship operations. Shows crew profiles. The Systems part deals with spaceship resources and engineering data. The Missions section helps organize mission tasks and track progress. The platform also has emergency training scenarios like dealing with oxygen or heart issues. The Systems section includes things like power and cooling systems. The project also looks at how to handle communication delays in space. The system uses types of sensors and technology to collect and process data. The design includes things like materials and ways to keep the astronaut comfortable. The digital version has dashboards, graphs and interactive controls. The project brings together areas of space support into one system. It looks at both the body and the spaceship as part of the mission. The team considered things like how the body changes in space how to make sensors accurate and how to keep the system reliable. They also looked at how to make the software easy to use. The system uses colors to show info and has text to explain what the colors mean. The emergency training is meant to help prepare astronauts without confusing it with medical situations. The project also includes ways to help with health like the Aura-Psy assistant. The goal is to make space travel safer and more comfortable for astronauts by combining health monitoring, training and mission management. The system is meant to help astronauts stay healthy be ready for emergencies and manage their work and health in space. It also shows how to organize data in one place even when communication is delayed. The project brings together different areas of science and technology to make space missions better for astronauts.
